_readme: Corrections to the mirrored OC model that cannot be derived from the export (#606).
Every entry here is a RECORDED OBSERVATION with its evidence written down, never an
inference the build could have made for itself. That is the whole point of the file:
the two upstream sources disagree in ways only a third check can settle, and once
settled the answer has to live somewhere durable. The probe sweep that produced the
ending->node mapping ran against tornprobability's live API and no longer runs, and
the tenant export carries only its RESULT (resolved/starved), not the per-ending
probabilities it decided from -- so a correction cannot be re-derived at build time.
Two kinds of entry, deliberately separate because they fix different things:
The API reports more endings than the flowchart draws terminals for, and the
surplus keys are additional labels for a terminal it already has. The alias
takes the target's node, so it prices from the same observations instead of
Crimes Hub numbers its endings by reward rank; tornprobability numbers them by
its own scheme. They usually agree, and where they do not, joining the published
reward by key name puts it on the wrong ending. A hub key named here is consumed
by the mapping and is NOT also joined to the ending of the same name.

_evidence: Crimes Hub's own simulator, all six CPRs at 75 (2026-09-07), against tornprobability
at the same crew. Crimes Hub draws four good terminals; tornprobability reports eight
good endings. The surplus four are not separate outcomes -- their mass belongs to
terminals the diagram already has, and the grouping is exact:
Crimes Hub  Good End #3  = node _B8S1_  17.78%
tornprobability  goodEnding3 10.526 + goodEnding35 6.316 + goodEnding310 0.936 = 17.778
Crimes Hub  Good End #4  = node _B8S2_   5.93%
tornprobability  goodEnding4  3.509 + goodEnding45 2.104 + goodEnding410 0.312 =  5.925
Good End #1 (42.10 vs 42.105) and #2 (14.03 vs 14.035) match one-to-one, as do all
three bad ends, so the two services agree everywhere except this grouping.
Left starved, those four sat at $0 while holding 9.67% of the crime's probability,
and because a starved ending is priced-by-definition (#473) the panel reported the
result as COMPLETE: a firm $111,028,512 where the answer is $122,489,526.
Crimes Hub publishes four good endings for this crime; the diagram draws four good
terminals; tornprobability reports six good endings. Matching the hub's published
respect against each terminal's OBSERVED respect identifies the join exactly:
node      observed respect    Crimes Hub
_A7S_          171            goodEnding1  170   (our goodEnding1)
_A7S2_         153            goodEnding2  155   (our goodEnding2)
_A5S_          137            goodEnding3  136   (our goodEnding3)
_B5S_          120            goodEnding4  122   (our goodEnding6)
So Crimes Hub's goodEnding4 is our goodEnding6. Joined by key name it landed instead
on our goodEnding4 -- which is starved, has no node, and is therefore the one ending
on the crime that can never carry an observation to check it against.
NOT FIXED HERE: our goodEnding4 and goodEnding5 are still starved and still sit at $0
while holding real probability. By the Blast from the Past precedent they are surplus
labels for terminals this crime already has, but which ones needs the same Crimes Hub
simulator check, and guessing would put invented money on screen.
